name: Clare Valley

climate: Shiraz and Cabernet Sauvignon sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: Australia's Geographical Indications nest in three levels: zones, the regions inside them, and subregions inside those.
keyfacts: Clare Valley was registered as an Australian Geographical Indication on 25 March 1999.
Vineyards sit at about ⟦elev|820 to 1,800 feet|250 to 550 m⟧, and large drops in temperature at night slow ripening.
Rain falls mainly in winter, averaging about ⟦rain|20 inches|510 mm⟧ a year, and the dry growing season leaves few disease risks apart from eutypa.
The region has no legally defined subregions, but it is informally split into Auburn, Clare, Polish Hill River, Sevenhill and Watervale.

notes: Clare Valley Riesling is restrained and austere when young, with lime and mineral notes, and it can evolve for decades.
Its Cabernet Sauvignon shows dark, rich black fruit with firm but plush tannins.

blurb.text: One of Australia's oldest wine regions, in the Mount Lofty Ranges zone of South Australia's Mid North, about ⟦dist|88 miles|140 km⟧ north of Adelaide and best known for Riesling. Plantings are above all Shiraz (39 percent), with Cabernet Sauvignon at 22 and Riesling at 21.
